tickets.title: Wire the worker processors — ALL SIX queues are inert, not just backfill
acceptance: Every queue in QUEUE has a registered processor: backfill (plan + entity pages), delta (webhook deltas), enrich, reconcile, snapshot (metric compute), dlq
The worker builds a ForgeProvider per workspace from the CONNECTION credential: decrypt via the vault, wrapped in the BudgetedClient so Law 7 holds for real ingestion
Honours FORGE_BASE_URL as the API does, so a self-hosted forge or a fake is reachable from the worker too
e2e: connect through the UI against the fake forge, the worker drains the queue, and the org overview renders data that arrived through INGESTION rather than the seeder
apps/api/test/wiring.test.ts KNOWN_INERT shrinks to [] — the gate fails if a queue is left behind
notes: Filed 2026-08-13. apps/api/src/workers/index.ts constructs the runtime with processors: {} and the comment 'Empty until W2-03 supplies the real entity processors' — but W2-03 is DONE, and processBackfillJob exists and is fully tested in packages/ingest. The processors were built and never registered, so THE WORKER CONSUMES NOTHING IN PRODUCTION. A customer connects, the API enqueues a plan job, and nothing ever drains it: no error, no data, just a dashboard that stays empty.

This is the FOURTH built-but-never-mounted defect found this week (SSE events W4-18, connections/sync/webhooks W4-19, now the processors) and the most consequential. The others made a feature unreachable; this one makes the core loop inert. Same cause each time: the unit tests mount the thing themselves into a throwaway scope, so the production wiring is exercised by nothing. Worth a standing check that every route plugin and every queue processor appears in the production entrypoint, not only in a test.

Deliberately NOT attempted at the end of a long session: the wiring requires decrypting stored forge credentials inside the worker and constructing a budgeted provider per workspace. That is security-sensitive integration, not mechanical plumbing, and starting it with little context left is how credential-handling mistakes ship.

SCOPE CORRECTED 2026-08-13 after a systematic audit rather than another accidental discovery. It is not just the backfill queue: the worker registers NO processors at all, so all six declared queues are inert — delta (so accepted webhook deliveries are never applied), enrich, reconcile, snapshot (so metric snapshots are never computed) and dlq as well as backfill. Re-sized 8 -> 13. The practical consequence is that waves W2 (ingestion, 5/5 done, 25 pts) and W3 (metrics, 13/13 done, 45 pts) are code-complete and fully unit-tested but NONE of that code executes in production: today's dashboard is a view over a warehouse the SEEDER fabricates, which is exactly why it looks healthy.

PARTIAL 2026-08-13: THREE of six queues wired, the core loop among them. apps/api/src/workers/processors.ts registers backfill (both the 'plan' fan-out and the entity-page jobs), delta (webhook deltas, accepted by the receiver since W2-04 and never applied until now) and snapshot (the metric numbers every screen reads). enrich and reconcile and dlq remain inert and are still on the wiring-gate KNOWN_INERT list, which shrank 6 -> 3.

CREDENTIALS: no new crypto was written. apps/api/src/workers/forge-provider.ts resolves a repo's connection row and calls the SAME credentials.decryptCredential the API uses; a second implementation of credential handling is a second thing to get wrong. It differs from the connect-time discovery provider in two deliberate ways: it goes through the BudgetedClient because Law 7 makes the rate-limit budget law for real ingestion (discovery skips it only because a connection row may not exist yet), and the SC-12 host allowlist is derived from the configured base URL so a self-hosted forge is permitted without widening it to a wildcard. A purged connection mid-backfill returns null and the job ends quietly rather than failing into the DLQ forever.

ROUTING DETAIL: the planner orders 'checks' alongside the paginated entities, but checks are fetched per-PR through the enrich lane, not walked page-by-page at repo scope — processBackfillJob only accepts PaginatedEntity. The plan processor routes the five paginated types and reports the rest as deferredToEnrich rather than dropping them silently. VERIFIED: the worker boots with real processors and reports healthz 200. NOT YET VERIFIED: data actually flowing end to end — that needs the worker running inside the e2e stack against the fake forge, which is the remaining piece of this ticket and of W12-02. Gate: lint 0, typecheck 0, test 0 (465/465), e2e 0 (37/37).

MEASURED 2026-08-13 rather than assumed, by running the worker against the fake forge and driving the real operator flow. RESULT: the PLUMBING works and the DATA FLOW is still unproven, and the reason is the fake, not the product. Evidence: connect + repo-select created fixture-org/alpha-service; the plan job fanned out into five per-entity jobs carrying the planner's own jobIds (bf-<id>-commits/-prs/-issues/-releases/-deployments); Redis shows 18 completed and 0 failed. But the repo sits at pending_backfill with 0 commits, 0 PRs and no sync_cursors, because e2e/helpers/fake-forge.ts only implements /user/repos and /hooks — every entity fetch 404d and the jobs completed against empty results.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE REMAINING WORK: it is smaller and better understood than 'run the worker in the e2e stack'. The fake forge needs entity endpoints (commits, pulls, issues, releases, deployments) returning fixture pages, and then the assertion is simply that alpha-service gains rows and flips off pending_backfill. ALSO WORTH CHECKING while doing it: a 404 from the forge produced a COMPLETED job with no error and no cursor. That is defensible for a genuinely empty repo but indistinguishable from a broken endpoint, and a backfill that silently completes against a 404 is exactly the kind of quiet failure this project keeps finding.

NARROWED 2026-08-13 to a single reproducible symptom, with the fake no longer the blocker. The fake forge now serves entity pages (commits/pulls in GitHub's REST shapes, parsed by the real normalize.ts) and sends x-ratelimit-* headers on every response, which GitHub always does and whose absence the BudgetedClient reads (Law 7). Neither change made rows appear. THE SYMPTOM, exactly: the plan job COMPLETES and returns {planned:5, deferredToEnrich:1} — so planning, the provider, credential decryption and the fan-out all work — but the five per-entity jobs go straight to BullMQ's DELAYED set and never execute. completed=1 (the plan), failed=0, delayed=5. processPlan adds them with a jobId and NO delay option, so the delay is not coming from the call site. Next session starts there: instrument or read why an add() without delay lands in delayed. Everything upstream is proven; this is the last link.

ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED 2026-08-13 (second session). The previous note above is WRONG and is left in place only so the mistake is not repeated: the five entity jobs did NOT sit unexecuted in the delayed set. They RAN, threw, and went to delayed awaiting exponential-backoff retry. The signature is unambiguous - attemptsMade=1 and delay=30000 exactly matching RETRY[ingest.backfill].backoff.delay; failed=0 only because attempts (5) were not exhausted. Nothing was injecting a delay at the call site, which is why none was ever found there. LESSON: read the job hashes in Redis (failedReason / stacktrace / atm) before theorising about queue state.

THE ACTUAL BLOCKER was SC-12. Every entity job died on ForgeSsrfError "scheme must be https, got http:" because the e2e fake forge is http://127.0.0.1:9099, which violates the guard three ways (http scheme, IP-literal host, not on the allowlist). Fixed with an operator-only, loopback-only escape hatch (allowInsecureLoopback, off by default, allowlist still enforced). Defensible because the forge base URL is NOT user input anywhere: it comes from the operator FORGE_BASE_URL env at the composition root and no route or UI accepts one, so an operator opting in gains nothing they did not already have. A LAN forge over plain http stays rejected - that is a separate posture decision for the founder.

TWO PRODUCTION BUGS found alongside, both independent of the test. (a) forge-provider.ts derived the SC-12 allowlist entry from URL.host, which INCLUDES the port, while validateBaseUrl matches URL.hostname, which does not - so any self-hosted forge on a non-default port (https://git.corp.com:8443) could never match its own allowlist entry. Invisible on api.github.com where 443 leaves host port-less, and squarely in D1a MVP scope. (b) Same class again: the allowlist compared against the bracketed IPv6 hostname WHATWG returns ("[::1]"), so a natural entry ("::1") never matched. Both sides normalized now.

THE FIFTH BUILT-BUT-NEVER-CALLED DEFECT, found here: plan/state-machine.ts defines the whole queued->history->enrichment->live lifecycle, is fully unit-tested, and had NO production caller - processBackfillJob invoked setRepoStatus only for paused_budget, so no repo had ever left pending_backfill. Wired now via a guarded UPDATE (concurrent entity jobs would make read-then-nextPhase() throw "illegal sync transition" and fail into the DLQ). Related: the metrics snapshot was enqueued by processPlan immediately after the fan-out, so it computed BEFORE any entity job wrote a row and every metric persisted as 0.000000 over an empty warehouse - the concrete reason the dashboard always looked healthy. It now fires from the all-entities-done hook, keyed on jobId.snapshot so BullMQ idempotency elects a single winner with no lock.

INGESTION NOW DEMONSTRABLY WORKS - the first real rows in the project history. fixture-org/alpha-service: 3 commits (REST) and 2 PRs (GraphQL), sync_status backfilling, all five sync_cursors backfill_done, backfill queue completed 6 / failed 0 / delayed 0, and the snapshot computed over real data (M7 = 24.0, dims {S:2} = the two ingested PRs). The fake forge also needed a POST /graphql handler: PRs are fetched over GraphQL, not the REST /pulls the fake already served.

VERIFICATION IS NOW AUTOMATED, which is the point given this ticket is the fifth instance of the pattern. The worker runs as a Playwright webServer using the SHIPPING entrypoint, so the assertion runs on every e2e run rather than only when someone starts a worker by hand; globalSetup flushes bull:* first, because the seeder issues fresh repo ids while jobs keyed to old ids survive in Redis and BullMQ jobId idempotency would let a run inherit an earlier success and report green while ingesting nothing. Negative control performed: flipping FORGE_ALLOW_INSECURE_LOOPBACK to 0 makes the new e2e fail with commits 0, so it can genuinely fail. Gate: lint 0, typecheck 0, 487 unit (was 465), 40 e2e (was 39), all exit 0.

STILL IN_PROGRESS, deliberately, and it is a small well-understood remainder. Acceptance requires ALL SIX queues registered and KNOWN_INERT shrunk to []; enrich, reconcile and dlq are still inert, so KNOWN_INERT is [enrich, reconcile, dlq] and the two-directional wiring gate still guards it. The core loop - the consequential part - is done and proven. The live phase is deliberately unreachable until the enrich processor lands, because enrichment_complete requires it and wiring history_complete straight to live would contradict INGESTION section 2. RECOMMEND splitting the remaining three queues into their own ticket so the proven core loop can close - that is a founder call, not one to make silently.

CARRIED FORWARD, unresolved: a 404 from the forge still produces a COMPLETED job with no error and no cursor - defensible for a genuinely empty repo, indistinguishable from a broken endpoint. Partially mitigated for the GraphQL path only (listPullRequestsGraphql now throws a diagnosable error when the endpoint returns no data at all, rather than a bare TypeError, and deliberately does not optional-chain into an empty page). The REST paths still complete silently on 404.

SPLIT PROPOSED 2026-08-13 and filed as W12-05 (enrich, reconcile and dlq processors). W12-03 as written demands all six queues and KNOWN_INERT == []; the core loop - backfill plan + entity pages, delta, snapshot - is wired, proven end to end and now guarded by an e2e that runs on every suite. Holding the ticket open for three unwired lanes hides that the consequential part is finished. If the split is accepted, W12-03 closes at 13 points with backfill/delta/snapshot done and W12-05 carries the rest; if not, W12-03 stays open until W12-05 lands. Not marked done unilaterally - re-scoping acceptance criteria is a founder call.

UNBLOCKED 2026-08-13 by W12-05. The "KNOWN_INERT shrinks to []" criterion is now satisfied - the list is empty, with dlq moved to SINK_QUEUES and asserted as a sink (fed by attachDeadLetter, consumed by nobody). The remaining literal mismatch is criterion 1, which lists `dlq` among the queues that must have a registered processor; that clause is incorrect by design, since a DLQ consumer would drain the failures the admin ops page exists to display (§6). RECOMMEND closing W12-03 with that clause noted as superseded by the sink assertion. Left in_progress rather than closed unilaterally, on the same principle as before: correcting acceptance is a founder call.

DONE 2026-08-13, founder agreement. Every criterion is met except the clause in acceptance 1 listing `dlq` among the queues requiring a registered processor, which is incorrect by design: attachDeadLetter feeds the DLQ and the admin ops page reads it (INGESTION §6), so a consumer would drain the failures it exists to preserve. That clause is superseded by the SINK_QUEUES assertion in apps/api/test/wiring.test.ts, which enforces the real contract in both directions — attachDeadLetter stays wired, and the sink stays unconsumed. KNOWN_INERT is [].

tickets.title: Wire the remaining three queues — enrich, reconcile, dlq
acceptance: enrich processor registered and consuming the payload INGESTION section 6 actually specifies: commitFiles {repoId, sha}, key en:{repoId}:{sha}. enrichCommitChurn already implements exactly this.

A PRODUCER enqueues those jobs — nothing enqueues enrich work today, so a processor alone would be a consumer for a queue nothing feeds (the same defect class this ticket exists to close). One job per ingested commit SHA that has no commit_files yet, keyed on jobId.enrich so a re-run collapses.

The fake forge serves the per-commit files endpoint, and the e2e proves enrichment END TO END by asserting M1/M2 go NONZERO for the ingested repo — churn metrics need commit_files, so a real number is stronger evidence than any fixture-served assertion.

reconcile processor registered AND fed: requeueErrorRepos is implemented with no caller, and section 6 specifies a nightly cron with key rc:{repoId}:{yyyymmdd}. A repeatable schedule is in scope — without it, reconcile is inert under a different name.

dlq is asserted as a SINK, not given a processor: attachDeadLetter must stay wired and the queue must have NO consumer. wiring.test.ts gains a SINK_QUEUES concept so this is enforced rather than allowlisted.

sync_status reaches `live`: define and implement what "enrichment queue drained" means per repo (section 2 states the transition but there is no per-repo cursor for enrich the way backfill_done exists), then run the state machine to its designed end.
wiring.test.ts KNOWN_INERT shrinks to [] with dlq moved to SINK_QUEUES — so "every queue is either consumed or an asserted sink" becomes true and stays true.
notes: Split out of W12-03 on 2026-08-13, after the core loop was wired and proven end to end. W12-03 registered backfill (plan fan-out + entity pages), delta and snapshot; these three remain inert and are tracked by the KNOWN_INERT list in apps/api/test/wiring.test.ts, which fails the build in BOTH directions (a queue with no processor that is not on the list, and a processor that landed without leaving the list).

THIS UNBLOCKS THREE THINGS beyond the queues themselves. (a) The `live` phase: plan/state-machine.ts routes enrichment -> live via enrichment_complete, which only the enrich processor can raise, so today a fully backfilled repo correctly stops at `backfilling`. Do NOT shortcut history_complete straight to live - that contradicts INGESTION section 2. (b) W12-02 acceptance 1: the fake forge deliberately does not serve reviews/checks yet, because nothing consumes them and an unverifiable fixture is the pattern this project keeps finding. (c) PR detail is currently rendering empty pr-reviews/pr-checks sections for ingested repos.

CARRY THIS ACROSS: a 404 from the forge still produces a COMPLETED job with no error and no cursor on the REST paths - defensible for a genuinely empty repo, indistinguishable from a broken endpoint. Only the GraphQL path was hardened (listPullRequestsGraphql throws a diagnosable error when the endpoint returns no data at all, and deliberately does not optional-chain into an empty page). The enrich lane adds more REST fetches, so decide the policy here rather than adding more silent-success surface.

ALSO KNOWN, and cheap to fix while in here: M1/M2 metric snapshots compute as 0.000000 for ingested repos because churn needs commit_files, which the fake forge does not serve. M7 correctly reads 24.0 from the two ingested PRs, so the snapshot path itself is proven - this is a fixture gap, not a metrics bug.

ACCEPTANCE REWRITTEN 2026-08-13 before any code was written. The original criteria were authored in-session without reading INGESTION sections 2/3/6 and contradicted the design in three ways. (1) They said enrich handles "per-PR reviews and per-head-SHA checks". It does not: section 2 defines enrichment as per-commit file churn, and the section 6 payload is literally commitFiles {repoId, sha}. CHECKS are a HISTORY-phase entity (section 3 entity order: PRs -> commits -> checks -> issues -> releases/deployments), not an enrichment one. (2) They demanded KNOWN_INERT == [] including dlq, but the DLQ must NOT have a processor — attachDeadLetter already routes exhausted jobs there and section 6 says they are surfaced on the admin ops page with a replay button, so a consumer would drain the evidence. (3) They ignored that reconcile is a nightly CRON, so a processor without a schedule feeds on nothing. Corrected in the ledger rather than built to, on the same principle applied to the handoff misdiagnosis.

CONSEQUENCE FOR W12-03: its acceptance also demands KNOWN_INERT == [], which is UNREACHABLE BY DESIGN because of the dlq sink. W12-03 therefore cannot close against its literal text no matter what W12-05 does. The SINK_QUEUES change here is what makes that criterion satisfiable for both tickets — worth doing first, since it changes what "done" means for two tickets.

OPEN DESIGN QUESTION FOR BRAD — reviews have no home. upsertReviews and provider.listReviews both exist and are fully built; neither appears in ENTITY_ORDER nor in any section 6 queue payload, yet sync_cursors permits a `reviews` entity_type. So PR detail renders an empty pr-reviews section for ingested repos and nothing in the design says which lane should fill it. Deliberately NOT resolved by picking a lane — that is a design decision, and inventing a home for it is how the entity order stops matching the doc. Same question applies to `checks`: it IS in ENTITY_ORDER (history phase) but processBackfillJob only accepts PaginatedEntity, because checks are fetched per head-SHA rather than walked page-by-page at repo scope. It needs a non-paginated history path, which is a real piece of design work rather than plumbing.

DONE 2026-08-13. All seven corrected criteria met and each verified rather than assumed. enrich: processor consumes the §6 commitFiles {repoId, sha} payload, and fanOutEnrichment PRODUCES those jobs from the history-complete hook keyed on jobId.enrich - the queue previously had neither end. reconcile: processor handles a `sweep` job (rescue errored repos via requeueErrorRepos, which had no caller since W2, then fan out per-repo jobs keyed rc:{repoId}:{yyyymmdd}) plus per-repo jobs running reconcileRepo, fed by a nightly repeatable job whose own jobId keeps N worker replicas to ONE schedule. dlq: left without a processor on purpose and asserted as a sink in wiring.test.ts. KNOWN_INERT is now [].

THE BUG THIS ALMOST SHIPPED WITH: the enrichment predicate was first written as `additions IS NULL`. That is wrong - the history backfill already populates additions/deletions from the list payload and stamps stats_source='graphql' (writers.ts), so the producer would have found nothing to do, enqueued nothing, declared enrichment drained immediately, and flipped the repo to `live` with M1/M2 still at zero. Caught by checking upsertCommits before trusting the column. The predicate is stats_source IS DISTINCT FROM 'detail', since only upsertCommitFiles writes 'detail' and only it writes the commit_files rows churn metrics read. Pinned by a test named for exactly this case.

MEASURED END TO END, and this is the strongest evidence the phase works: fixture-org/beta-web reaches sync_status `live` with 4 commit_files rows, and the churn metrics that were 0.000000 for the first ingested repo now read M1 = 94.0 (dims {net: 62, rework: 68}) and M2 = 0.954842. M7 stays 24.0. Two snapshots per repo is correct, not duplication: one when history completes and one after enrichment drains - metric_snapshots is an append-only time series read newest-first, and the early partial snapshot is what FR-WEB-8 describes (dashboard usable from enrichment onward, churn-dependent metrics labelled partial until it finishes).

NEGATIVE CONTROLS, both against the full path rather than a filtered run: unregistering the enrich processor fails the e2e with commit_files 0 (Expected 4, Received 0) and the repo stalls at `backfilling` instead of reaching `live`. The reconcile sweep has its own test asserting an errored repo is re-planned, a live repo is swept under the §6 idempotency key, and a repo still backfilling is deliberately NOT swept (reconciliation repairs data meant to be complete; racing an in-flight backfill would fight its cursors).

STILL OPEN AND STILL FOR BRAD - reviews have no lane in the design. upsertReviews and provider.listReviews are both fully built and called by nothing; reviews appear in no ENTITY_ORDER and no §6 payload, yet sync_cursors permits the entity_type. PR detail therefore renders an empty pr-reviews section for ingested repos. `checks` is a related but distinct gap: it IS in ENTITY_ORDER (history phase, §3) but processBackfillJob only accepts PaginatedEntity because checks are fetched per head-SHA rather than walked at repo scope, so it needs a non-paginated history path. Neither was resolved here - picking a lane for either is design work, and inventing one is how the code stops matching the doc.

tickets.title: Broaden enrichment to per-parent detail fetches; survive un-hookable repos
acceptance: Enrichment covers per-PR reviews and per-head-SHA check runs alongside per-commit churn, per the founder decision of 2026-08-13
sync_status `live` requires BOTH halves of enrichment drained, not just churn
The fake forge serves reviews and check runs, closing W12-02 acceptance 1
PR detail renders pr-reviews and pr-checks for an ingested repo, asserted in e2e
Webhook registration failure is non-fatal, so a public repo the operator does not administer still backfills
notes: FOUNDER DECISION 2026-08-13: broaden enrichment from "per-commit file churn" to "per-parent detail fetches". Reviews (per PR number) and check runs (per head SHA) are nested fetches keyed on a row the history phase already ingested — structurally identical to commit churn and unlike every paginated history entity, which is walked page-by-page at repo scope. This resolves the inconsistency where INGESTION §3 listed `checks` in the HISTORY entity order even though processBackfillJob only accepts PaginatedEntity precisely because checks cannot be walked that way. No new queue: ingest.enrich already carries the right priority and retry policy, so this adds job kinds (commitFiles, prDetail).

upsertReviews and upsertCheckRuns were both fully built, fully tested and called by NOTHING until this ticket — the sixth instance of that pattern here. The visible symptom was PR detail rendering an empty reviews section for every ingested repo.

SCHEMA: added pull_requests.enriched_at (migration 0004, one additive nullable column). A per-PR marker, NOT a repo-level high-watermark: enrich jobs run concurrently and complete out of order, so a watermark could advance past PRs that never ran and report enrichment drained — flipping the repo to `live` with reviews missing. Counting child rows cannot work either, because a PR with genuinely zero reviews AND zero checks would look permanently pending and hold the repo at `backfilling` forever.

WEBHOOK REGISTRATION IS NOW NON-FATAL, and this was a real bug rather than test convenience. The repo row is inserted BEFORE registerWebhook and enqueuePlan comes AFTER, so an unguarded throw left the repo parked in pending_backfill with no work ever queued — stuck silently and permanently. It fails legitimately in two supported cases: a PUBLIC repo the operator does not administer (hook creation needs admin, which reading does not imply — exactly the founder smoke test), and a SELF-HOSTED install with no publicly reachable URL (D1a), where deliveries could never arrive anyway. Webhooks are a freshness optimisation; backfill loads the history and the nightly reconcile sweep repairs what a missed delivery would have carried. The failure is recorded on repos.last_error ("live updates unavailable — …") rather than swallowed, so a lagging repo is explainable.

FIXTURE BUG CAUGHT BY AN EXACT COUNT: check runs were given per-PR ids restarting at 1, and check_runs upserts on (repo_id, kind, forge_run_id, run_attempt) — so PR 12's "build" silently overwrote PR 11's and only 2 of 3 rows landed. A >0 assertion would have passed. Ids are globally unique now.
Measured: fixture-org/beta-web reaches `live` with 3 reviews, 3 check runs, 4 commit_files, 3 commits and 2 PRs; both PRs carry enriched_at. Gate: lint 0, typecheck 0, 495 unit, 40 e2e, all exit 0.

tickets.title: Auth rate limit (SC-11) makes the unit gate intermittently red
acceptance: The full unit suite passes repeatedly (10 consecutive runs) with no auth-related failures
The fix does not weaken SC-11 in production — the limit stays 10/min/IP where it matters
notes: OBSERVED 2026-08-14. `pnpm test` failed 3 tests in apps/api/src/routes/repos/index.test.ts with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'value')", then passed 497/497 on an immediate re-run with no code change. The error is at the LOGIN step, not on data: the helper reads the oauth_state cookie off the authorize response and gets undefined, which is what a 429 looks like from that call site.

CAUSE (high confidence, not yet proven): SC-11 caps the auth flow at 10 requests per minute per IP. Vitest runs test FILES in parallel and several of them perform a real OAuth round trip against the same in-process app from the same address, so a burst can exceed the cap. e2e/global-setup.ts already documents this exact hazard and works around it by logging in ONCE for the whole Playwright run — the unit suite has no equivalent.

WHY IT SURFACED NOW: nothing in the limiter changed. W12-05/W12-06 added four test files (completion, enrich-queue, graphql, processors.reconcile), which shifts scheduling and makes the burst more likely. It is latent, not new — and it is the worst kind of red, because it points at a repo route that has nothing to do with the failure.

DO NOT fix by raising the limit globally: SC-11 is a real control (T-13/T-14 brute-force). Options worth weighing: share one authenticated session across the API route tests the way globalSetup does for e2e; make the limiter keyed per test-app instance so parallel files do not share a bucket; or make the limit configurable and set it high ONLY under NODE_ENV=test, which is the least good option because it stops exercising the control.

NOT introduced by the reconcile-sweep incident and not fixed by it — those are separate. Filed rather than fixed inline so the gate reliability work is visible instead of being absorbed into an unrelated ticket.

DONE 2026-08-14. Root cause NOT definitively proven, and that is stated deliberately rather than glossed: the flake fired once in roughly four runs beforehand and has not reappeared in 11 consecutive runs since, which is strong but not conclusive. What WAS proven is that the helper hid the evidence. Five test files each carried a copy of loginAs built entirely on non-null assertions, so any unexpected auth response surfaced as "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading value)" from a repo-route test — an error naming neither auth nor a status code, which is exactly why it could not be diagnosed after the fact.

TWO CHANGES. (1) One shared helper at apps/api/src/testing/login.ts that asserts each step and reports the actual status, with a message naming the SC-11 limit as the likely cause of a 429. If this recurs it will now say so instead of pointing at the wrong subsystem. (2) The helper CACHES the session per app instance and per user. Each login costs two requests against /auth/*, which is capped at 10/minute (AUTH_FLOW_RATE_LIMIT), and the metrics and connections suites sat exactly ON that cap at five logins each — any extra request tipped them over. Caching drops most files to two auth requests total. This mirrors what e2e/global-setup.ts already does (one login per run) for the same documented reason.

SC-11 IS UNTOUCHED. The limit is still 10/min/IP in production and the rate-limit test still exercises it directly. The fix removes needless auth traffic from the suite rather than weakening the control — raising the cap under NODE_ENV=test was considered and rejected, since it would stop exercising a real security control precisely where it is cheapest to test.
VERIFIED: 11 consecutive full unit runs, 497/497 each, zero failures (acceptance asked for 10). Plus lint 0, typecheck 0, e2e 40 passed + 1 skipped.

tickets.title: pnpm setup: one command from clone to a ready dev stack
acceptance: A single `pnpm setup` on a clean clone leaves the dev data tier healthy, migrated and seeded
It WRITES .env from the template and GENERATES TOKEN_ENC_KEY and SESSION_SECRET rather than leaving them blank
It is idempotent: running it twice is safe and never overwrites an existing .env secret
It fails with an actionable message when podman/node/ports are missing, naming what to do
notes: FILED 2026-08-18 after auditing the fresh-clone path by actually running it. Booting the API with only .env.example dies twice: first `missing required env var GITHUB_APP_CLIENT_ID`, then `TOKEN_ENC_KEY is required (32-byte hex)`. Both blanks are CORRECT (Law 9 — a committed key is a published key), which means the documented setup file cannot start the app and never could.
Generation, not documentation. Telling a newcomer to run `openssl rand -hex 32` twice and paste the results is the step everyone gets wrong; the script should do it and print what it did.
NEVER overwrite an existing secret in .env. A rerun that regenerates TOKEN_ENC_KEY silently makes every stored forge credential undecryptable (DEPLOYMENT.md §3).

Port preflight matters here specifically: a compose dev stack already holds 3000 on this machine, which is what E2E_API_PORT exists to work around. A setup script that does not check ports hands the user a confusing failure later instead of a clear one now.

DONE 2026-08-19. scripts/setup.mjs: tool checks (node 22+, podman or docker), .env creation, secret generation, data tier up, wait for postgres to actually ACCEPT connections, migrate, seed, then print what is still missing.

THE COMMAND IS `pnpm bootstrap`, NOT `pnpm setup`. `pnpm setup` is a pnpm BUILTIN ("Sets up pnpm") and wins over a package script, so every doc telling a newcomer to run `pnpm setup` would have quietly run pnpm's own command and never touched this repo. Caught by running `pnpm setup --help` before wiring the name.

FOUND AND FIXED, a real security defect rather than a setup inconvenience: .env.example PRE-FILLS SESSION_SECRET and WEBHOOK_SECRET with `dev-insecure-…` placeholders. A fill-only-blanks rule therefore left every fresh install signing session cookies and validating webhook HMACs with a secret PUBLISHED IN THIS REPOSITORY — forgeable by anyone who has read it. Placeholders (dev-insecure/REPLACE_WITH/changeme) now count as unset and are regenerated; .env.example says so.

NEVER OVERWRITES A REAL SECRET. Regenerating TOKEN_ENC_KEY on a rerun would silently make every stored forge credential undecryptable (DEPLOYMENT.md §3) — damage that surfaces weeks later as "why can we no longer sync". Verified: rerunning leaves .env byte-identical.

SECOND BUG FOUND BY RUNNING IT: the readiness probe shelled out to `podman exec -T postgres`, but the compose SERVICE is `postgres` while the CONTAINER is `repopulse-postgres`, and plain `podman exec` has no -T. It reported "Postgres did not become ready" against a database that had been healthy for six days. Now `podman compose -f compose.dev.yaml exec -T`.

DOES NOT INVENT GITHUB CREDENTIALS. GITHUB_APP_CLIENT_ID/SECRET identify an OAuth app only a human can register; a generated value would produce a stack trace at login instead of an honest "you have not set this". Setup ends by naming the gap and pointing at demo mode (W13-02).

VERIFIED BOTH PATHS: (A) fresh directory with only .env.example -> .env created, all three secrets generated as valid 32-byte hex, rerun leaves the file unchanged. (B) this repo -> idempotent, migrations applied, warehouse seeded (3 repos, 24 commits, 15 PRs, 1536 snapshots). Gate: lint 0, typecheck 0, 589 tests zero skipped, three validators exit 0.

tickets.title: Demo mode: run the whole app with no GitHub account and no OAuth app
acceptance: With DEMO_MODE on, a fresh install serves a usable app: log in, see seeded org/repo/PR/file screens, no GitHub OAuth app registered anywhere
The fake forge is reachable outside the Playwright harness — a runnable process, not a test-only fixture
DEMO_MODE HARD-REFUSES to start when NODE_ENV=production, and a test proves the refusal
The demo login is visibly a demo: the UI says so, and it cannot be reached when DEMO_MODE is off
notes: CHOSEN BY THE USER 2026-08-18 over a real local-password login, deliberately: password auth is new security surface (session handling, credential storage, SC-11) and this is being written unattended. Demo mode reuses code that already exists and is already tested.

The pieces exist but are trapped in e2e/: e2e/server.ts boots the API against a fake forge with OAuth mocked at the boundary, and seedWarehouse() fills the warehouse deterministically. Promote, do not rewrite.

THE REFUSAL IS THE SECURITY CONTROL. A demo login that can be switched on in production is an authentication bypass. It must fail closed — refuse to boot, not silently disable — and the test must assert the refusal, not just the happy path.
Demo mode must never touch a real forge. C1/Law 4 still applies: it reads our own Postgres, seeded, and any forge call goes to the local fake.

DONE 2026-08-19. `DEMO_MODE=1 pnpm dev` serves the whole product with no GitHub account and no registered OAuth app: fake OAuth boundary, fake forge, seeded warehouse. Verified as a real login round trip with GITHUB_APP_CLIENT_ID/SECRET deliberately REMOVED from the environment — /auth/login -> fake authorize -> /auth/callback issues repopulse_sid, /me/context returns 200 with demo:true, /repos returns seeded repos with health scores.

A SEPARATE ENTRYPOINT (apps/api/src/demo.ts), not a DEMO_MODE branch in index.ts. e2e/server.ts already documents why: pointing the shipping binary at a fake forge is not a capability production should have. A branch inside index.ts would create exactly that capability and put it one environment variable away. Demo composes the SAME buildApp — every plugin, guard, route and session path is the one that ships; only the three OAuth URLs and the forge base URL differ.

THE FAKES MOVED OUT OF e2e/ into packages/shared/src/testing/fake/{forge,github}.ts, re-exported from @repopulse/shared, and the four e2e importers now take them from the package. A fixture only a test runner can start cannot serve a demo.

REAL BUG FOUND BY RUNNING IT: demo.ts first took apiBaseUrl from API_BASE_URL, which .env pins to http://localhost:3000. Running the demo on any other port therefore built an OAuth redirect_uri pointing at whatever ELSE was listening on 3000 — here, the deploy/compose stack — so the callback 307d to /login and issued no session. A login that appears to do nothing, with nothing in the log to explain it. apiBaseUrl is now derived from the port actually bound; demo mode is local by definition.

THE REFUSAL IS THE SECURITY CONTROL AND IT FAILS CLOSED. assertDemoAllowed throws under NODE_ENV=production BEFORE any port is bound or fake started, and the message says why (authentication bypass) so nobody deletes the check as noise. Four unit tests cover it, including that explicit falsey spellings (DEMO_MODE=0/false/empty) count as OFF — a truthiness check on the string alone would enable a demo login in front of real data. Also checked as a real process: `NODE_ENV=production DEMO_MODE=1 tsx apps/api/src/demo.ts` refuses.

THE UI SAYS SO, AND THE SERVER IS THE AUTHORITY. /me/context carries `demo`, the shell renders a banner from it, and the banner tests pin absent-vs-false: an API that omits the field renders NOTHING rather than treating unknown as demo (a fake-data warning over real numbers) or as not-demo. A browser build flag was rejected — the browser cannot know what forge the API it is talking to is connected to.
GATE: lint 0, typecheck 0, 597 unit tests (was 589), zero skipped, e2e 56 passed + 1 skipped, three validators exit 0.

tickets.title: pnpm dev: api + workers + web in one command
acceptance: `pnpm dev` starts the API, the ingestion worker and the web dev server together with distinguishable prefixed logs
The worker gets a start script of its own — today nothing in any package.json launches it
Ctrl-C stops all three cleanly, leaving no orphan process holding a port
A port already in use is reported as such, before the stack half-starts
notes: FOUND 2026-08-18: apps/api/src/workers/index.ts is the ingestion process and NOTHING in any package.json starts it. The only thing that launches it is playwright.config.ts webServer. So a developer running `pnpm --filter api dev` gets an API whose queues fill and never drain — the same silent-inertness class this project has now caught eight times.
Three terminals is not a setup story. One command, or people run the API alone and conclude ingestion is broken.

DONE 2026-08-19. scripts/dev.mjs spawns api + worker + web with prefixed, colour-coded output, and apps/api gained the dev:worker and start:worker scripts it never had. No new dependency: three spawns and a readline prefix is less code than wiring a process runner, and it keeps the shutdown semantics ours.

TWO REAL BUGS FOUND BY RUNNING IT, not by reading it. (1) `pnpm --filter` runs each child with cwd=apps/api or apps/web, so the child's own `import 'dotenv/config'` looks for .env in THAT directory and finds nothing — the API died on "missing required env var DATABASE_URL" and the worker on "DATABASE_URL and REDIS_URL are required", on a machine where .env exists and every other entrypoint works. Fixed by loading dotenv in the PARENT and inheriting. playwright.config.ts carries a note about the identical trap. (2) Port 3000 is held on this machine by the deploy/compose.yaml stack, so the preflight fired on its first real run.

TWO PREFLIGHTS, env before ports, because a fresh clone hits the env wall first: missing vars are reported as a list with the fix (`pnpm setup`, or DEMO_MODE for no GitHub account) instead of a stack trace interleaved with two other processes' output. Ports are checked BEFORE anything starts, so a conflict never leaves two orphans running.

One process exiting takes the stack down, and anything still alive 3s after SIGTERM gets SIGKILL — a half-running stack is the failure mode where the worker is silently absent and people conclude ingestion is broken.

VERIFIED: all three up, /healthz 200 on api (:3010), web 200 (:5173), worker 200 (:3001), Ctrl-C clean with no orphans. Missing-env path and port-conflict path both checked. Gate: lint 0, typecheck 0, 589 tests zero skipped, three validators exit 0.

NOT FIXED HERE, and it is the newcomer blocker: the API still requires GITHUB_APP_CLIENT_ID/SECRET to boot at all, so on a fresh clone `pnpm dev` cannot start the API even with a database. That is W13-02 (demo mode). The preflight message points at it rather than pretending otherwise.

tickets.title: Dedup key collapses findings that differ only in digits
acceptance: The evidence normaliser stops stripping digits, or the key stops relying on a digit-stripped quote: CVE-2020-11023 and CVE-2020-11022 on one package must be TWO findings, proven by a test that fails against the current normaliser
Every other reason the normaliser exists — volatile whitespace, line numbers that shift, timestamps — keeps working, with a test per case so the fix does not simply delete the normalisation
A migration path for rows already collapsed is stated: either they re-open on the next scan or the ticket says plainly why they cannot
notes: FOUND BY W8-06, not by review. The scanner agent hit it building the dependency scanner: two CVEs on the same package normalise to the same dedup key, so the second silently becomes an occurrence of the first. It worked around the symptom by carrying the vulnerability id in ruleId, which the scanner branch of the key includes verbatim — the underlying normaliser is untouched and SHARED by every dimension.

The risk is not limited to CVEs. Any two findings that differ only in a number are at risk: two complexity findings quoting different measured values, two EOL findings quoting different cycles, two log lines differing by a port.

FIXED AT THE CAUSE, narrowly. The rule is now: a token containing a LETTER is an identifier and keeps its digits; a token of only digits and punctuation is a number and loses them. : and brackets separate, while - _ . join — which is how these strings are actually written, so app.ts:42 still loses its line number while cve-2020-11023 and log4j-core keep their identity.

Seven tests hold all three properties at once: the two CVEs stay apart, every reason the stripping existed still works (line numbers, shifted constants, leading line numbers, reflowed whitespace), and the normaliser stays idempotent — one that is not gives a single finding two keys.

THE MIGRATION SHIPPED WITH THE FIX because it had to: dedup_key is stored and the next scan recomputes it, so changing the normaliser would have made affected rows unreachable — duplicate inserted, original swept as resolved, occurrence counts and triage decisions detached. rekeyFindings recomputes in place, proven against live Postgres to preserve the row id, a confirmed status and an occurrence count of 7.
It REPORTS collisions rather than resolving them: when two rows now key identically, choosing a survivor is a decision about someone triage history, not something a migration should do quietly.

tickets.title: Wire the performance pack: findings must take dimension `performance`
acceptance: A scanner OWNS the perf pack and emits its findings with dimension 'performance' — W9-08's fourth acceptance criterion, which is currently unmet
An integration test proves a bpm-perf-* rule fires on the perf fixtures and lands as a STORED finding with dimension 'performance'

The logging scanner's cost is documented rather than changed: it never paid for the perf rules — readRulepack does not recurse, so the perf SUBDIRECTORY was invisible from the parent dir it points at. The premise of the original criterion was wrong.
notes: FILED 2026-08-21 from a product-gap review. W9-08 is marked DONE and its fourth acceptance criterion reads: 'findings take dimension performance and ride the standard triage/verify/plan rails'. They do not.

EVIDENCE, all grep-verifiable. (1) rulepacks/code-health/perf/perf.v1.yaml holds 8 bpm-perf-* rules. (2) The ONLY runtime loader of that directory is scanners/logging/run.ts:152, which points semgrep at the whole code-health pack dir. (3) At run.ts:164 it does `if (!finding.ruleId.startsWith('bpm-log-')) continue;` — so every perf finding semgrep produces is evaluated and then DISCARDED. (4) The only other reference to `bpm-perf-` in apps/ or packages/ is perf-pack.test.ts, which reads the YAML off disk and asserts its contents; it never runs a scan through the product's pipeline.

CONSEQUENCES: no scanner emits dimension 'performance' (the chainer passes it through but can only chain findings that already exist), so the Findings Explorer's performance facet is permanently empty and the performance risk axis at apps/api/src/routes/risk/index.ts:31 can never grade. VISION.md names performance as one of four review dimensions; three of the four ship.

The rules are NOT the problem: written for RepoPulse with per-rule provenance, trigger and clean fixtures, and messages that deliberately refuse to quote speedup multipliers. This is wiring, not authoring.
This is the disconnected-pipeline defect (anti-slop R-26) inside the codebase of the product built to find it.

WRITE_SCOPE WIDENED to apps/api/src/workers/** on purpose. A scanner that no schedule invokes is the exact defect this ticket exists to fix — the perf pack was already a component nothing mounted, and shipping a perf SCANNER nothing calls would move the disconnection up one level rather than removing it. Same precedent as routes/repos/$repoId/route.tsx's RiskAxisStrip widening in W10-05. It joins the existing weekly snapshot pass, so it costs no extra tarball.

CORRECTION TO THIS TICKET'S OWN EVIDENCE, made while implementing it. The filed note said the perf findings were 'evaluated and then DISCARDED' at logging/run.ts:164. They were not evaluated at all: readRulepack lists a directory and keeps its .yaml files WITHOUT recursing, so from rulepacks/code-health/ it loaded anti-slop.v1.yaml and logging.v1.yaml and never saw the perf/ subdirectory. The conclusion held — no perf finding could ever reach storage — but the mechanism was wrong, and acceptance 4 was written on the wrong premise. Verified by running readRulepack over both directories; both facts are now pinned by a test that needs neither a database nor a sandbox.

tickets.title: persistFindings dies on two same-key findings in one batch — logging_hygiene fails on any file with two console.log calls
acceptance: Two findings in ONE batch that share a dedup key fold into one stored finding instead of raising a unique-constraint error
The fold is reported in PersistResult, never silent — a scanner must be able to say how many it collapsed

A regression test proves three same-key findings in one batch fold to one stored row rather than raising; the shipped logging_hygiene scanner is verified by hand against a file with two console.log calls, the case that fails today
occurrenceCount still counts RUNS, not in-batch duplicates: a file with twenty matching lines must not add twenty sightings per scan
notes: FILED 2026-08-21 mid-W9-13, which it blocks. Found by running the new perf scanner: 8 findings from one fixture file, two sharing a dedup key, whole scan failed.

ROOT CAUSE, packages/insights/src/findings/store.ts:113 — byKey is built ONLY from rows already in the database. The loop then inserts every batch finding whose key is not already stored, so the first of an in-batch pair inserts and the second violates findings_workspace_repo_dedup_key. The catch marks the scan run failed and NOTHING is stored.

THIS IS NOT A NEW-SCANNER PROBLEM. Verified against the SHIPPED logging_hygiene scanner (W9-04) on a three-line file containing two console.log calls: status failed, findingsCreated 0, same constraint error. Every deterministic scanner builds evidenceQuote as `<file>:<line> — <ruleId>`, and dedupKey buckets lines by ten, so two hits of one rule in one file collide whenever they fall in the same ten-line window. NOT every pair in a file — the first draft of this note said that and it is wrong — but a cluster of matching lines a few apart is the ordinary case, and it is the one that fails.

The dedup keys own semantics say the fold is correct: same key means same finding. What must NOT happen is inflating occurrenceCount by the number of duplicate lines — that field counts sightings across runs.

The scanner writes 'code_health' at scanners/anti-slop/run.ts:123,144,174,218. The findings are real; they are filed under the wrong name, so the `slop` facet returns nothing while the rows sit in Code Health.

Without a migration the next scan finds no match, inserts a duplicate, and the sweep resolves the original — taking its occurrence count and triage decisions with it. tickets.title: Local accounts: scrypt, first-admin bootstrap, forced password change
acceptance: Email + password using Node built-in scrypt — no third-party hashing dependency (D10/D14) — with constant-time verification
First admin created on first boot from ADMIN_EMAIL/ADMIN_PASSWORD, idempotent, and the account must change its password before reaching anything else
Wrong password and unknown email are indistinguishable in both response and timing; the existing auth rate limit applies
No self-service signup exists; an admin creates users
notes: scrypt from node:crypto — no hashing dependency to licence or redistribute (D10/D14) and no native module to build. Parameters live IN the stored hash, so cost can be raised later without invalidating anyone; a correct password against weaker params reports needsRehash and upgrades on login. N=2^15 needs maxmem above node default 32 MB — verified by running it, not assumed.

Unknown email, wrong password, and a federated account whose address was guessed all perform one full derivation against a decoy hash and return the same reason-free failure. Timing asserted in a test, not asserted in prose.

The forced-change gate is the SHAPE of the session: a pending user holds pendingPasswordChangeUserId instead of userId, so every guarded route rejects it without having heard of the gate. Stated limit: it cannot revoke an already-issued session.

ensureBootstrapAdmin is idempotent on "any local account with a password exists" rather than on the email, so editing ADMIN_EMAIL later does not mint a second admin. It THROWS on a weak ADMIN_PASSWORD — a fresh install whose only credential is "admin" should stop and say so.

PROVEN END TO END with no GitHub App configured: boot logs bootstrap:created, /auth/login 404s, local login returns must_change_password, the gated session gets 401 from /api/v1/me/context, and after the change the same session reads 200 as admin.

THE STARTUP VALIDATOR CAUGHT MY OWN GAP: the API still refused to boot because W11-02 marked GITHUB_APP_CLIENT_ID required — a requirement D14 had removed. Both are now optional and the GitHub routes only mount when set; authRoutes still registers because it owns the shared session.

tickets.title: Generic OIDC: discovery, PKCE, ID-token verification
acceptance: Discovery, authorization-code + PKCE and the code exchange are ours (plain HTTPS); ID-token verification uses jose (MIT) against the provider JWKS
Rejects, each proven separately: bad signature, wrong issuer, wrong audience, expired, alg=none
Claims map to auth_subject and email; works against a fixture IdP in tests with no network
Configured entirely from env; an unconfigured deployment simply does not offer the button
notes: Discovery, PKCE (S256 only) and the code exchange are ours — plain HTTPS, the same shape as the existing GitHub flow. jose (MIT, verified) does only the cryptography: JWKS and signature verification. That split is D14 written down.

The five rejects each have their own test. alg=none is built with UnsecuredJWT because SignJWT refuses to emit one — a test using SignJWT would have proved nothing, and the test asserts the header really says none.
auth_subject is the IdP sub, never the email: email is reassignable at most companies, and using it would let a new employee inherit a departed one account.
Zero network in the suite — an in-process fixture IdP mints tokens against a generated keypair, and the route test exercises the real remote-JWKS path over loopback.

The author listed what is NOT implemented rather than letting silence imply conformance: at_hash/c_hash, UserInfo, refresh tokens, RP-initiated and channel logout, request objects, JWE, max_age/acr/amr, hybrid and implicit flows, PKCE plain (rejected on purpose).
Registered only when configured; a PARTIAL configuration throws at boot on purpose, because the alternative is failing at the callback after the user has already authenticated with their IdP.

notes: Split from W15-06 deliberately: three substantially different auth mechanisms, none of which is a base-URL-plus-key. Do not fold back in.

NOT BLOCKED ON CREDENTIALS — I said that on 2026-08-28 and it was wrong. Re-reading the acceptance: all four criteria are about the auth MECHANISM, not a live vendor round-trip. SigV4 is a pure signing function and AWS publishes official test vectors (aws-sig-v4-test-suite) that verify it with fake keys. Vertex's service-account flow is JWT construction and signing, testable with a throwaway RSA key plus a fake token endpoint. The device flow is an HTTP dance, testable against a fake authorization server — this repo already fakes GitHub's OAuth boundary in e2e/helpers/fake-github.ts. The fourth criterion (an unsupported kind fails at CONFIGURATION time) needs nothing at all.

What genuinely needs credentials is only a live smoke against the real vendor, and this repo already has the pattern for that: smoke-real-forge.spec.ts is opt-in behind SMOKE_REAL_FORGE=1 and skips otherwise. So the work is claimable now; only the final vendor smoke waits on Brad.
PREMISE CHANGED — verified against the live vendor docs 2026-08-28 (Law 2), and two of the three mechanisms are not what this ticket assumed.

BEDROCK NO LONGER NEEDS SigV4. AWS now exposes an OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API at https://bedrock-runtime.{region}.amazonaws.com/openai/v1/chat/completions, authenticated by EITHER SigV4 or an Amazon Bedrock API key sent as `Authorization: Bearer` (AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK). That is base-URL-plus-key — exactly what this ticket's own note said it was not — so it runs on the existing openai_compatible transport with no new dependency and no signing code. Acceptance criterion 2 as written ('authenticates via the AWS credential chain (SigV4)') would have us build ~100 lines of HMAC plus a dependency decision for no capability the API key does not already give. Flagged for Brad rather than implemented as specified.

VERTEX is OpenAI-compatible too: https://{location}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/{project}/locations/{location}/endpoints/openapi/chat/completions with `Authorization: Bearer <access token>`. But the token is SHORT-LIVED (about an hour) and minted from a service account, so this one does need the async, refreshing auth seam — a pasted token would expire the same day it was configured.

THE SEAM: requestHeadersFor() is synchronous and static. Vertex needs a cached expiring token and the device flow needs a refreshing stored one, so auth has to become async and per-request. Per-request rather than per-build, because createGatewayResolver caches a WorkerGateway for 60s and a token minted at build time would be correct only by accident of that TTL.

DEVICE FLOW (copilot, openai_subscription) is the honest split: it needs a human at a browser once per install, so it can never be exercised by `pnpm test` or `pnpm e2e:demo` at all — a different class of blocker from the other two, and a different surface (an interactive route plus a write-back path into the encrypted columns, which hostsFromProviders does not have).
DO NOT flip `supported: false` -> true for a kind that cannot complete a real call. That is the dependency_cve mistake (W16-36): a criterion met while the capability is absent.

BLOCKED 2026-09-08: explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for the standalone product release (IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md §1, "unfinished non-API-key model authentication"). API-key providers ship; Vertex AI, Bedrock and Copilot auth do not. Parked, not abandoned, and not done.

DEFERRED 2026-09-23, founder decision on the v1 self-host release: moved OFF the release path explicitly (it was already out of scope per IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md §1). API-key providers ship in v1. Stays blocked, not done.

notes: Found in W16-10. Several suites delete users, and at least one clears repos outright, so a file reading seeded rows passes or fails on FILE ORDER. Three attempts failed before W16-10 was made to own its whole fixture chain (workspace, user, forge connection, repo) — correct for that file, but a workaround rather than a fix, and repos.connection_id being NOT NULL makes the chain expensive to repeat.

Also seen earlier in this wave: packages/ingest dlq.integration fails whenever a dev worker is running, because it shares the dev Redis and the worker steals the poison message before the test can assert on it. The ports doc separates HTTP ports but nothing separates the queues.

NOT A SIGHTING — CORRECTED 2026-08-28. The 15 failures across accounts.test.ts + auth/local.test.ts that were first written up here as a file-order flake were a deterministic W16-13 regression: identities.user_id references users with NO ON DELETE, and W16-13 gave the demo account an identity, so both `deleteAllLocalUsers` helpers threw 23503 and failed every test in their file after any `DEMO_MODE=1 pnpm dev`. Fixed in the helpers.

STILL OPEN, and the real content of this ticket: packages/auth accounts.test.ts and apps/api routes/auth/local.test.ts BOTH delete every row matching `users WHERE auth_provider = 'local'`, because the bootstrap's idempotence rule is genuinely global ('does ANY local account exist'). Two files owning one global predicate is a latent race whatever the FKs do. A pg_advisory_lock is the obvious mutex and is NOT trivial here: createDb returns a postgres.js POOL, so a lock taken on one connection can be released on another — it needs a reserved connection held for the file's lifetime. Bigger than the 3 points on this ticket.

RESOLVED 2026-08-28, and the ticket's PREMISE was wrong. Files do not run in parallel: `fileParallelism: false` is honoured, proved with a probe that appended start/end timestamps from three files in three packages and showed no overlapping windows. So this was never a concurrency race — it was ORDER, plus two specific bugs.

The two real breakages, both reproduced and both fixed: (1) the identities.user_id FK, which was a W16-13 regression, not a flake; (2) dlq.integration ran on the shared dev Redis under BullMQ's DEFAULT prefix on the real `enrich` queue name, so a `pnpm dev` worker consumed the poison message before the assertion — and its afterAll obliterate wiped the developer's actual enrich queue. Now namespaced with prefix 'repopulse-test'. Verified by running the full suite WITH the demo stack up, which is the state that broke it twice.

Also migrated vitest.workspace.ts into `test.projects` in vitest.config.ts. The workspace file is deprecated and due for removal, and `fileParallelism: false` is load-bearing — losing it silently would activate the one remaining hazard below.

REMAINING, dormant: packages/auth accounts.test.ts and apps/api routes/auth/local.test.ts both delete every `users WHERE auth_provider = 'local'`, because the bootstrap's idempotence rule is genuinely global. Harmless while files are sequential, a race if fileParallelism is ever turned on. Documented in vitest.config.ts beside the setting that keeps it dormant.
